title: Soft Pull-Apart Dinner Rolls
subtitle: a pan of tender, buttery milk-and-egg rolls that tear apart warm from the oven
imageAlt: A pan of golden, buttery pull-apart dinner rolls on a navy napkin
servingsNote: 12 rolls: 2 each with dinner, and more for sandwiches the next day

beforeYouStart.text: The milk should be warm, not hot: about 40–45°C (it feels warm on your wrist). Hotter can kill the yeast.
Most of the time is rising (about 1½ hours, included). Find a warm spot, like the oven with just the light on.

steps.title: Warm the milk
steps.text: Heat the milk and butter until the butter melts, then cool until just warm, 40–45°C.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk 3 cups of the flour with the yeast, sugar and salt. Add the warm milk mixture and the egg and stir into a shaggy dough. Add the remaining ½ cup flour a little at a time, only as much as needed for a soft dough that pulls away from the bowl.

steps.title: Knead
steps.text: Knead on a lightly floured counter 8 minutes (or 5 in a stand mixer with the dough hook), until smooth and slightly tacky.

steps.title: First rise
steps.text: Put the dough in a greased bowl, cover and let rise in a warm spot about 1 hour, until doubled.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Grease a 9×13 pan. Divide the dough into 12 pieces (about 70 g each) and roll each into a smooth ball. Set them in the pan in 3 rows of 4.

steps.title: Second rise
steps.text: Cover and let rise 30–40 minutes, until puffy and touching. Meanwhile heat the oven to 190°C (375°F).

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 18–22 minutes, until deep golden and they sound hollow when tapped (90°C / 195°F inside).

steps.title: Butter
steps.text: Brush the hot rolls with the melted butter. Cool 10 minutes in the pan, then pull apart.

fixIt.fix: The milk was too hot or the yeast was old. Check the date, and keep the milk at 40–45°C.
Too much flour went in. Stop adding flour once the dough is soft and just tacky.

fixIt.problem: Tops browning before the centre is done
fixIt.fix: Lay foil loosely over the pan for the last 5 minutes.
Weigh the pieces. About 70 g each gives 12 even rolls.

saleTip: Yeast keeps for months in the freezer; buy the 3-pouch strip or a jar when baking supplies go on sale in December.
swap: Active dry yeast: same amount. Dissolve it in the warm milk with 1 tsp of the sugar and wait 5–10 minutes until foamy before mixing; the rises can take a little longer.
leftovers: Split and toasted for leftover-roast sandwiches, or cubed and dried for stuffing.
doneness: Deep golden tops and 90°C (195°F) in the centre roll on an instant-read thermometer.
source: Based on tested soft dinner roll methods (Robin Hood, King Arthur Baking): an enriched milk, butter and egg dough with instant yeast, baked at 190°C (375°F).
prepAhead: Overnight: after shaping, cover the pan and refrigerate up to 18 hours. Let it sit at room temperature 45–60 minutes until puffy, then bake.
Bake ahead and freeze the cooled rolls up to 3 months.
reheat: Wrap in foil and warm at 180°C (350°F) 8–10 minutes.

basic.note: A lean dough: no egg and no butter brush.

0-0.name: milk
0-0.note: plus 3 tbsp, to replace the egg

stepNotes.1: Basic: no egg; the extra milk takes its place.

fancy.note: Garlic-Parmesan butter brushed on the hot rolls.

stepNotes.7: Fancy: stir the extra melted butter and garlic powder into the butter before brushing, then sprinkle with the Parmesan.

plating: Serve right in the pan, wrapped in a tea towel.
Soft butter in a small dish alongside.

why.0-6: Egg makes the rolls richer, softer and more golden.
why.0-4: Sugar feeds the yeast and keeps the crumb tender.
why.0-0: Milk fat gives the soft, fine crumb dinner rolls are known for.

funFact: Rolls baked touching each other stay soft on the sides because they steam one another; that's the whole trick behind pull-apart rolls.

keeps.note: freeze cooled rolls in a bag
keeps.thaw: On the counter about 1 hour, then warm in foil

pairs: for ham sandwiches the next day
